The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

events.title: Team RIVER Volunteers
events.description: Volunteer with Team RIVER (Randall’s Island Volunteer Ecological Restorers) and help keep Randall’s Island Park beautiful! Team RIVER Volunteers regularly work with the Natural Areas team twice a month to take care of and restore our natural spaces on the island. With our Horticulture team, volunteers care for the many gardens, green streets and meadows, every second Wednesday of each month. Team RIVER also works with our Sports Field and Operations teams, keeping our park clean and maintained. If you are only able to volunteer on a limited basis, you are still very much welcome!This volunteer opportunity is open to individuals from the community. Groups of more than 5 people must contact: Volunteers@RandallsIsland.orgVolunteers must be at least 11 years old. Anyone under the age of 18 must have a waiver signed by their legal guardian before starting any work. Children under 16 must also have an adult with them while volunteering. A downloadable volunteer waiver can be found at this link: General Volunteer – Randall’s IslandRegistration is required here.Location: Volunteers will be notified after registration.For inquiries about accessibility, to request an accommodation, or for event information, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org.

events.title: Cuidado de Árboles y Arbustos para Jardineros Comunitarios
events.description: Únase a GreenThumb para un Taller Práctico de Cuidado de Árboles en el jardín comunitario. Juntos, exploraremos los árboles y arbustos del jardín mientras aprendemos maneras prácticas de identificar árboles, evaluar su salud, reconocer señales de estrés o enfermedad, comprender sus necesidades de agua y del lugar donde crecen, y practicar técnicas básicas de poda y mantenimiento. También dedicaremos un momento a conectarnos con los árboles como elementos fundamentales del ecosistema del jardín: desde sus raíces y ramas hasta sus flores, frutos, semillas, aves e insectos. El taller concluirá con la participación de todos en la plantación y el riego de un nuevo árbol de serbal de servicio (serviceberry), seguido de una breve reflexión colectiva para darle la bienvenida al árbol al jardín.Esta sesión está abierta a cualquier persona que hable inglés, ya que tanto nuestro facilitador como el personal son bilingües.Regístrate AquíNYC Parks GreenThumb organiza este evento. Nos enorgullece ser el programa de jardinería comunitaria urbana más grande del país, apoyando a más de 550 jardines comunitarios en toda la Ciudad de Nueva York. Con el apoyo de GreenThumb, los jardines comunitarios son espacios que promueven la justicia ambiental y contribuyen a que nuestra ciudad sea más equitativa, segura y verde para todas las personas. Los eventos de GreenThumb son gratuitos y están abiertos al público.

events.title: Gardening with Ground Covers
events.description: Have you ever wanted an alternative to woodchips or landscape fabric? If so, this is a workshop for you. Ground covers are an excellent way to protect exposed soils while also providing habitat and improving soil stability. In this workshop we will explore a variety of garden situations, plants and expand the definition of “ground covers.” Participants will learn how to select, establish and design with ground covers. No matter the size of your garden, ground covers are a great step towards building a sustainable and more resilient community garden.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Extend Your Growing Season with Low Tunnels
events.description: Urban gardening doesn’t have to stop when temperatures drop! This workshop will teach you how to build low tunnels to protect cold-hardy crops and extend your growing season in small spaces like community plots, backyards, and rooftops. Learn which winter crops thrive in NYC’s climate and how to choose and use materials that fit tight urban gardens. Gain practical, space-efficient skills to construct sturdy low tunnels so you can keep growing fresh produce through the winter.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Working with Rain: A Rain Garden Workshop
events.description: This workshop aims to introduce attendees to the Rain Garden Stewardship Program, sponsored by the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEP). During the workshop, attendees will learn about the purpose and function of rain gardens, as well as the dos and don'ts of stewarding one. events.title: Candlelight Ghost Tours
events.description: Doors slam, floorboards creak, voices call into the dead of night. Venture into “Manhattan’s Most Haunted House” by flickering candlelight to hear chilling – and true – tales of decades of otherworldly activity in the house, the results of years of paranormal investigations – and the latest stunning scientific findings.The Tredwell family lived at 29 East 4th Street for nearly 100 years, and at least eight people died in the house. Reports of strange and inexplicable occurrences have been widespread since Gertrude, the last surviving Tredwell, died in 1933. Is it Gertrude who is watching over her family home? Join us and decide for yourself.50-minute tours begin every half hour, 6:30 to 9 p.m.

Mounting fact-based evidence points to the very likely reality of paranormal activity at the Merchant’s House.Join paranormal investigator Dan Sturges on a 90-minute In-Person Super Spooky Candlelight Ghost Tour for an in-depth look at the latest research and findings. events.title: Saunksquas, Sassafras, and Moccasins: Walking Tour with Oleana Whispering Dove
events.description: Join Oleana Whispering Dove for a walking tour on the Wave Hill Grounds, highlighting the rich legacy of the region’s Indigenous Saunksquas and the profound impact of these women throughout history. This tour reflects on historical imprint of known figures like Sojourner Truth, Maya Angelou, Condoleezza Rice, Susan B. Anthony, Matilda Cage, Lucretia Mott, and Gloria Steinem with earlier unsung female leaders known as Saunk Squa’s; Mama Nuchwe, Dostou, Wastawancett, Lyssie, Annetie Pownock. These Native American women held the highest-ranking leadership roles in their communities and were honored by European settlers with titles like Her Royal Majesty, The King’s Queen, and Indian Princess—recognizing their powerful status and influence as they played a pivotal role in governing their regional tribes, leading land negotiations, and signing land treaties. Walks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. A limited amount of walking sticks are available to borrow. Pace varies from a slow walk to moderate walk throughout.

events.title: The Art of Noticing: A Mindful Birding Experience
events.description: Join nature educator Ryan Mandelbaum and yoga/mindfulness instructor Susie Caramanica to explore how mindfulness can deepen our awareness, observation, and enjoyment of the natural world. This guided experience combines mindfulness practices with birding, inviting participants to slow down, clear mental distractions, and become more fully attentive to the environment around them. Through simple grounding exercises, participants will cultivate a focused awareness that can help them notice more—from a bird's song to subtle movement in the canopy, participants can fully appreciate an encounter that might otherwise go unnoticed. The program begins with gentle mindfulness practices designed to settle the mind and sharpen sensory awareness. Participants will then be guided through the landscape, learning to identify birds by sight and sound while observing behavior, habitat, migration, and seasonal activity. No prior experience with birding or mindfulness practice is necessary. Participants are encouraged to wear comfortable clothing and bring water and binoculars if they have them. Registration encouraged; online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251; drop-ins based on availability. Questions? Please contact us at information@wavehill.org or by calling the number and extension provided above. Following this program, join us for Yoga in the Garden with instructor Susie Caramanica (additional fees apply).Additional Fall 2026 Birding programs:Sun, Nov 8: November BirdingWalks follow a route along mixed-material pathways with varying elevations. events.title: Meet the Artists: Melanie Brewster and Noormah Jamal
events.description: Join us for a Meet the Artist program with exhibiting artists Melanie Brewster and Noormah Jamal. At 2PM, Brewster will be in conversation with Curator of Visual Arts, Rachel Raphaela Gugelberger, to discuss her Sunroom project, A Metaphysical Quest for the Deepest Backbend. This exhibition constructs a metafictional world in which a woman’s yoga practice has become so extreme that she transforms into an ouroboros: a serpent consuming its own tail, a symbol of cyclical time and eternal return. The exhibition takes place in the aftermath of this transformation, and Brewster aims to reflect on extreme wellness practices, the limits of enlightenment, and questions of access within contemporary wellness industries. At 3PM, Jamal will discuss her outdoor installation, Blooms, and activate the site with a collaborative poetry reading with NYU professor and poet Sonya Posmentier. In Blooms, flowering ceramic heads emerge from an arid landscape. These heads represent the resilience of a people through times of hardship, paying specific homage to Jamal's home of Peshawar, Pakistan. Once known as “City of Flowers,” over the years, Peshawar has become dry, mountainous city, and the people and landscape have both endured the effects of climate change and war. Still, the people persevere in their homeland, becoming the city’s flowers. Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. As part of the Sunroom Project Space, this program is designed collaboratively with the artists and takes various forms. Meet the Artist offers visitors, the artists’ communities, and others an opportunity to gain insight into the artist's creative process and the themes present in their work. Registration encouraged but not required, online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251.

Participants will take part in a light stewardship activity by helping remove vines from protected tombstones, supporting ongoing efforts to preserve these important landmarks.
events.venue: Victory Boulevard and Alberta Avenue (in Sylvan Grove Cemetery)

events.title: Healthy Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a relaxing, easy walk along the paved paths of Silver Lake Park. This gentle hike is ideal for all ages and abilities, offering a chance to enjoy fresh air, light exercise, and the park’s scenic views at a comfortable pace.
events.venue: Forest Avenue and Silver Lake Park Road (in Silver Lake Park)

events.title: Creatures of the Night: Bats
events.description: As the night falls, our fuzzy bat companion rises. Let the Urban Park Rangers be your guide as we learn more about these precious winged friends.
events.venue: Entrance - 215th Place and 33rd Road (in Crocheron Park)

events.title: Autumn Meditation Hike
events.description: On World Mental Health Day, release some stress as the Rangers guide you through meditation activities amongst reclaimed grasslands. As we hike and explore this hidden gem, we will be reflecting on letting go of emotional “left-overs” and finding gratitude in the upcoming winter.
events.venue: Archery Field Parking Lot (in Willowbrook Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Fort Totten
events.description: Its Open House New York Weekend! This hidden gem was a military base for over 100 years. Explore the many historic structures of the peninsula and learn about the important role Fort Totten played in New York City’s defense history, from the Civil War to today. Visit OHNY to register.
events.venue: Fort Totten Front Gate (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Family Camping: Staten Island
events.description: We camp to create lasting memories, connect with the natural world, and bond with our families. The Urban Park Rangers celebrate the tradition of camping and we look forward to welcoming your family. Families are chosen by lottery. Lottery registration opens on Monday September 28.
events.venue: Blue Heron Nature Center (in Blue Heron Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Fort Totten
events.description: Its Open House New York Weekend! This hidden gem was a military base for over 100 years. Explore the many historic structures of the peninsula and learn about the important role Fort Totten played in New York City’s defense history, from the Civil War to today. Visit OHNY to register.
events.venue: Fort Totten Front Gate (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Dubos Point Wildlife Sanctuary Wetland Cleanup
events.description: Volunteer with the Stewardship Team to protect coastal areas in Dubos Point Wildlife Sanctuary! Volunteers will help us remove the debris from the park, creating a healthier ecosystem. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers, please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.
events.venue: Bayfield Avenue and B65 Street (in Dubos Point Wildlife Sanctuary)

events.title: Volunteer Workday: Howard Garden
events.description: Join Howard Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a hands-on volunteer day building new garden beds--no power tools needed! This is an exciting project to be a part of. We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks.Join us for the whole project!Day 1 (Wed. Oct. 7) – Garden Site PrepDay 2 (Sat. Oct. 10) – New Bed BuildingDay 3 (Wed. Oct. 21) – Filling Beds & PlantingHoward Garden was founded in the late 1980's by community activists and artists who've made a lasting impact in the Brownsville community. These gardeners are still active to this day, and are excited to pass along the knowledge and skills gained through decades of environmental stewardship. This is a great opportunity for beginner and seasoned volunteers looking to join a growing garden!Register here!In the event of inclement weather, we'll reschedule this event to Sunday, October 11th.For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov. This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
events.description: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information. Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side? On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence. You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. events.title: The History of the Ouija Board
events.description: Dive into the history of the enigmatic Ouija board, and learn how spirit communication became a phenomenon that swept the nation. Today a trademarked game owned and manufactured by Hasbro, Ouija has a history that stretches back to the 19th century. At one time, the "talking board" outsold Monopoly—appearing in silent films, Valentine's Day greeting cards, popular sheet music, and even a Norman Rockwell illustration. Get an up-close look at more than a dozen vintage boards—all with their own unique design and aesthetic—that have dazzled the curious and mystified skeptics for more than one hundred years. When:October 11 | 7:00 pm - 9:00 pmWhere: Carpenter’s Shop (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

events.title: New Dendrology at the Arsenal Gallery
events.description: New Dendrology is a group exhibition featuring eleven artists whose work contributes to the study of trees, offering new insight and connection between humans and their arboreal neighbors.From communing with streets trees through a reading with The New York City Street Tree Tarot deck by Matthew López-Jensen, to the commitment ceremonies officiated by Laura Nova, artworks featured in this exhibition invite you to engage in a new kind of relationship with trees. Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova. Image credit: The Bright Oak, 2019, Matthew López-Jensen

events.title: Pelham Bay Park by Bike Tour
events.description: Have you ever wanted to go on a long bike ride in the Bronx but were worried about sharing the road with cars? Fret not! Join the Urban Park Rangers on a 9-mile bike ride through Pelham Bay Park that is almost entirely on dedicated bike trails. Bring water and a snack!
events.venue: Pelham Bay Nature Center (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: Indigenous People Day: The Siwanoy
events.description: Pelham Bay Park was once inhabited by small camps of coastal native people loosely referred to as the “Siwanoy” or “Southern People”. The Siwanoy traded along a route similar to the path of the Siwanoy trail. Hike with the Urban Park Rangers along this historic route and learn about the Siwanoy’s history and way of life.
events.venue: Bartow-Pell Mansion Museum (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: Nocturnal Insects Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on an evening of nocturnal insect exploration and learn about the many different insect species that emerge as sun begins to set earlier!
events.venue: Van Cortlandt Nature Center (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.title: Family Camping: Bronx
events.description: We camp to create lasting memories, connect with the natural world, and bond with our families. The Urban Park Rangers celebrate the tradition of camping and we look forward to welcoming your family. Families are chosen by lottery. Lottery registration opens on Monday October 5.
events.venue: Van Cortlandt Nature Center (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.title: Historic New York: Orchard Beach
events.description: Discover NYC's storied past with our expert Urban Park Rangers as your guide to historical events, people, and communities that have shaped our city and Parks. Join the Urban Park Rangers on a journey through time and learn the history of Pelham Bay Park’s Orchard Beach!
events.venue: Section 2 Orchard Beach (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: The Myth of Joe Two Trees
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers in a discussion about the Bronx classic The Last Algonquin while hiking through where the book is set, Pelham Bay Park! Participants will explore the facts and fiction surrounding the story of Joe Two Trees, purportedly the last Lenape person who lived in New York City. All participants welcome, even those who haven’t read the book!
events.venue: Section 2 Orchard Beach (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: It's A Horse of Course Hike and Greet
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a meet-up with our Mounted Unit and their horses! Meet a real horse officer at the Horse of Course program and discover the vital role of horses in city parks enforcement. Learn about how the NYC Parks Mounted Unit cares for the horses, where they live, what they eat, and how the Rangers and Mounted Rangers work together to keep the parks safe. The visit will be followed by horse related crafts in the nature center.

events.title: Prehistoric New York
events.description: Take a trip back in time with the Urban Park Rangers as we hike through Pelham Bay Park discussing the lay of the land in prehistoric times. Learn more about fossils and some geological highlights of New York City.
events.venue: Pelham Bay Nature Center (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: Tai Chi with Pin Pin Su
events.description: Tai chi—the ultimate mind and body workout, often described as “meditation in motion”—involves slow, fluid, continuous movements through formalized postures of centuries-old Chinese Taoist martial arts.This event is free and open to the public. All levels are welcome. Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes to move around in.Advance registration is encouraged. Walk-ups are welcome. The event will be canceled if it rains. The decision will be made by 5pm the day before and registrants will receive an email if the event is canceled.
events.venue: Under the Standard (in The High Line)

events.title: Brazilian Movement with Maria Assis
events.description: Come join us to dance on the High Line! Brazilian movement is a unique and fun combination of Samba reggae from Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, and West African and Latino beats. All levels are welcome.This event is free and open to the public. All levels are welcome. Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes to move around in. Water will be provided.Advance registration is encouraged. Walk-ups are welcome. The event is rain or shine—the event space is fully covered. In the event of extreme weather, this program may be canceled for the health and safety of our visitors and staff. If a cancellation is necessary, Eventbrite registrants will be notified via email and we will post an update on our website.

events.title: Spotlight tour: Art
events.description: Take a deep dive into the sculptures, billboards, murals and other art installations on and around the High Line with a 90-minute specialized tour led by a High Line Docent, a knowledgeable volunteer guide. In it, you’ll learn more about the artists and ideas behind the artworks specially commissioned for the High Line Art program.Art tours will be led by docent Tom Morris on September 10 and October 8.

events.title: "The Light That Shines Through the Universe": Lectures and Meditations - Monuments to War
events.description: As part of the public programming for Tuan Andrew Nguyen’s High Line Plinth commission, The Light That Shines Through the Universe, the High Line presents a monthly lecture and guided meditation series at the Spur. Presented in partnership with the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, the series invites visitors to engage more deeply with themes central to Nguyen’s work. Each session features a lecture by a scholar, artist, or cultural leader, followed by a guided meditation led by an invited practitioner.The series is hosted by Tashi Chödrön, Himalayan Programs and Communities Ambassador at the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, who, in her two decades with the Rubin, has led meditation programs for over ten years and is the current host of the Rubin’s Mindfulness Meditation podcast. Through this combination of intellectual and contemplative practice, the series invites audiences to pause, reflect, and consider the artwork’s historical and philosophical themes through both thought and experience.Closing the series, Nico Rodriguez, deputy director of Monuments Lab, considers Nguyen’s work alongside contemporary artistic approaches to memorialization. The discussion explores how artists reimagine monuments to war by transforming sites of violence into spaces for remembrance, reflection, and collective healing.The lecture will be followed by a guided meditation by Steve Clorfeine, a meditation teacher from the Shambhala tradition with over 40 years of experience.Rain date: October 11, 2 – 3pm

events.title: Historic Harlem Parks Super Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on a hike from Morningside Park through St. Nicholas Park and ending at the Northern tip of Jackie Robinson Park. Learn about the history, geology, and ecology of these beautiful parks.
events.venue: Manhattan Avenue and West 110th Street (in Morningside Park)

events.title: Saltwater Fishing
events.description: Want to go fishing but don’t know how or where to start? Join our Urban Park Rangers for free lessons! Learn how to properly use a fishing rod. Our experienced Rangers teach the ethics of fishing and the ecology of our waterways. All equipment will be provided. Recommended for ages 8 and older.
events.venue: 125th Street and Marginal Street (in West Harlem Piers)

events.title: Nature In A Warming World
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a focused walk through Inwood Hill Park to explore how climate change is affecting local plants and wildlife. Learn how shifting temperatures and extreme weather influence the insects, trees, birds, and mammals we see every day, and discover the changes already underway in this unique urban forest.
events.venue: West 218th Street and Indian Road (in Inwood Hill Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Mount Morris Fire Watchtower
events.description: A prominent feature of Marcus Garvey Park and its neighborhood, the historic Mount Morris Fire Watchtower serves as an important landmark for the Harlem community. Urban Park Rangers discuss the significance and history of this recently restored structure. Open access from 1pm to 2:45pm.
events.venue: Mount Morris Fire Watchtower (in Marcus Garvey Park)

events.title: Open House New York: The Highbridge Water Tower
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on a tour inside the iconic Highbridge Water Tower to learn about the history of New York City's water supply and enjoy the panoramic views from the top of the 200-foot tower Arrive between 1:00 p.m. and 2:45 p.m, to gain admittance. Registration is not required.
events.venue: West 174 Street and Amsterdam Avenue (in Highbridge Park)

events.title: Historic New York: Vaudeville Stars of the Evergreens Cemetery
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers in exploring one of Brooklyn’s hidden gems, the Evergreens Cemetery. Learn about the many famous performers from the vaudeville era onwards buried here, and the fascinating history of why they came to rest here.

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
events.venue: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.
events.venue: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)

events.title: The Garden People: 45 Years in Bloom
events.description: Since 1981, The Garden People have lovingly cared for this special corner at 91st Street in the heart of Riverside Park. What began as a grassroots effort by neighbors has blossomed into an iconic New York City landmark and a beloved refuge for community members and visitors. Join us as we celebrate 45 years of growing together and say thank you to the neighbors, volunteers, friends, and supporters who have helped our garden thrive. Enjoy an afternoon of live music and community amid the beauty of the garden.All are welcome. Come celebrate!

events.title: Sachet making + Community Engagement Tea
events.description: Stop by the garden for a tea tasting opportunity and herbal sachet making.

events.title: Pumpkin Painting at Newport Garden
events.description: Newport Garden and GreenThumb welcomes all for an afternoon activity! We will have limited pumpkins available for participants to paint. Come learn more about the garden and meet community members!

events.title: Children's' Harvest Festival
events.description: The Children’s Harvest Festival is a fun, hands-on event that celebrates the fall harvest and the importance of local agriculture. Children participate in seasonal activities such as harvesting crops, planting, and engaging in farm-based games and learning experiences. The festival promotes healthy eating, environmental awareness, and a deeper connection to where food comes from.

events.title: Open House New York: Gravesend Cemetery
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! The Urban Park Rangers will guide you through this landmarked cemetery that was established by Lady Deborah Moody in 1643 and is home to graves of early settlers and founding families of Brooklyn. Register at Open House New York.

events.title: Hispanic Heritage Month: Revolutions Across the Americas
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a discussion on the history of independence movements throughout the Americas in honor of Hispanic Heritage Month. Explore the chronology of Latin American revolutions, the evolving identity of American Latinx, and the connections between these stories and New York City. Standing near the site of the first sparks of the Battle of Brooklyn, we’ll reflect on how struggles for sovereignty—from the past to the present—continue to shape communities locally and globally.

events.title: Birding with Ryan
events.description: Join local birdwatching author and garden member Ryan Goldberg for a fall birding event. We'll check the garden's trees for migrating birds and the skies for passing hawks, and we'll also talk about birding in the city and the wonders of migration. Bring binoculars if you have them.

events.title: Volunteer Workday: Wanaqua Garden
events.description: Join Wanaqua Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a volunteer day helping repair garden beds and paint picnic benches! This community garden is cared for by volunteers who are excited to meet you and share their rich history of environmental stewardship, urban gardening, and hosting community events. This is a great opportunity for anyone looking to join a growing garden!No experience necessary - beginners are welcome! We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note some tasks will involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here!For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Open House New York: Ecology Park
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! Join the Urban Park Rangers at Ecology Park to learn about habitat restoration and ecological improvement. Discover native plant communities unique to New York City, and how to support these ecosystems in our urban landscape. Registration is required. Visit Open House New York to register

events.title: Open House New York: Prison Ship Martyrs' Monument
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! Discover the history of this Brooklyn landmark that pays tribute to the 11,000 men, women, and children who died on British Prison Ships during the Revolutionary War. Registration is required. Visit Open House New York to register
events.venue: Fort Greene Park Visitor Center (in Fort Greene Park)

events.title: Open House New York: Grand Army Plaza
events.description: It's Open House New York Weekend! Join the Urban Park Rangers and the Prospect Park Alliance for a special access tour of Prospect Park's Grand Army Plaza, including going inside the Soldiers’ and Sailors’ Memorial Arch and climbing the spiral stairs to the top. Registration only through Open House New York.

events.title: Volunteer Garden Workdays
events.description: Interested in being a garden volunteer? Fill out our Garden Interest Form!Join us every third Saturday from 11 AM-2 PM for our Membership Meeting and Volunteer Workdays! This is a great opportunity to learn about how we care for and manage George Washington Carver Community Garden. This Fall, we're making exciting progress to redesign the garden so that by spring, we're ready for the new growing season!We'll be dismantling old garden structures and moving organic material to prepare for our special Halloween Volunteer Event** where we welcome everyone to come in their best garden-themed costume & help us build our new beds!Fall Schedule (11 AM-2 PM):September 19thOctober 17thOctober 31st at 10:00 AM**November 21stFor questions, please e-mail us at gwashingtoncarvergarden@gmail.com. Follow us on Instagram where we'll share our exciting progress!

events.title: Soundview Park Forest Restoration
events.description: Volunteer with the Stewardship team to protect the forested areas in Soundview Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been funded in part by NYC Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

events.title: Seton Falls Park Plug and Shrub Planting
events.description: Join the Stewardship Team as we restore forested areas in Seton Falls Park with a plug and shrub planting! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work, learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health, and be trained in proper planting techniques. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been funded in part by NYC Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.
events.venue: Boller Avenue & Crawford Avenue (in Seton Falls Park)

events.title: Inwood Hill Park Forest Restoration
events.description: Volunteer with the Stewardship Team to protect the forested areas of Inwood Hill Park! Volunteers will contribute to ongoing restoration work and learn the importance of species diversity to ecosystem health. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty. Face masks may be worn at your discretion. Space is limited and registration is required. Volunteers under 18 must be accompanied by a chaperone. This event has been made possible with funds from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service. To sign up a group of 10 or more volunteers please reach out to stewardship@parks.nyc.gov.

events.title: Sharing and Gratitude
events.description: Amboy Street Garden will be holding a day of Sharing and Gratitude. In celebration of garden manager, Tammy Hall’s, thirty years as a professional storyteller, gardeners are invited come hear and share stories, bring toiletries and clothing for a barrel to be sent to Jamaica to support a community greatly affected by the recent hurricane, and enjoy refreshments, harvesting and fun!

events.title: East Village Music Festival
events.description: La Plaza will be hosting a day of music, food and kids activities celebrating the creative spirit of the East Village.

events.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
events.description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

events.title: The Perfume of Grief With Julianne Zaleta
events.description: Join perfumer and botanist Julianne Zaleta for this hands-on essential oils and perfume class surrounding the theme of grief.Significant loss demands real attention to your well being. Having a scent to support you won't cure grief, but the right composition will help you acknowledge and commemorate, perhaps even celebrate, disentangling loving memories from the pain of loss. It helps you honor and celebrate your memories, while easing the pain that comes with longing for a lost loved one. Plants can help so much in supporting and building the heart to be whole again, helping us find strength, courage and relief. Explore the oils associated with healing emotional pain and create your own perfume to take home.alchemologie.com

events.title: Author Talk with David Rocco: Fireboats of the FDNY
events.description: For the last century and a half, FDNY fireboats have played a vital role in protecting New York City’s waterfront. On Thursday, October 8, the Bayside Historical Society welcomes author and photographer David Rocco for an illustrated presentation exploring the history and evolution of these remarkable vessels.With more than 500 miles of shoreline, New York City has long relied on specialized fireboats to respond to fires along the waterfront and aboard ships. Using historic photographs and images, Rocco will trace their development from the early wooden-hull tugboats to the highly specialized vessels that serve the city today.Rocco has been involved in numerous historic preservation and cultural projects throughout the Hudson Valley and New York City. In 2023, he prepared the successful nomination that placed the retired FDNY fireboat John D. McKean on both the State and National Registers of Historic Places. He currently serves as Vice President of the Fireboat McKean Preservation Project.The presentation will be followed by a question-and-answer session and book signing.Admission is $10 for BHS members and $15 for non-members. Purchase tickets on the BHS website: https://www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/author-talk-with-david-rocco-fireboats-of-the-fdny.This event is part of Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.
events.venue: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)

events.description: Please note: this event has been cancelled.Grab a blanket and come enjoy a movie in a neighborhood park or playground! NYC Parks will host family-friendly movie showings across the five boroughs. Movies begin at dusk. Estimated start time is approximately 8:30pm. For more information visit nyc.gov/parks or call 311. events.title: REIMAGINING: Fall Get-Together
events.description: The event will begin with a moving live performance by musician Juan Usera and The Sambuco Tribe, setting the tone and making space for remembrance and renewal. Following the music, Bronx-based artist Tijay Mohammed will lead an interactive chalk art project aptly named “Message to my Ancestors,” transforming the pathway into a vibrant canvas that honors history and sparks imagination for the future.Local artists will work alongside Tijay Mohammed, including Adrienne George, Musah Swallah, Noel Hefele, and Yoshiko Mori.This unique gathering blends art, music, and community in a powerful act of reimagining, bringing people together in a shared experience of creativity and remembrance.Tijay Mohammed's "Message to my Ancestors" project is sponsored by Bronx Council on the Arts and AnkhLave Arts Alliance, Inc.The event is made possible by the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of the Office of the Governor and the New York State Legislature. This event is part of Van Cortlandt Park Alliance’s REIMAGINING initiative. VCPA invites the community to reimagine the park’s Enslaved African Burial Ground site as a memorial space that fosters long-term healing and restoration. Phase 1 of this project was supported by a generous grant from the Mellon Foundation. Juan Usera is a fourth-generation Bomba practitioner and culture-bearer from Santurce, Puerto Rico, a community educator, researcher, college professor, musician, and performer. He specializes in Puerto Rican and Caribbean music and culture and has over 20 years of experience developing highly engaging cultural activities and arts programs throughout the New York tri-state area. Juan is the founder and director of La Tribu del Juey Sambuco (La Tribu), an Afro-Caribbean music and dance ensemble and arts in education company. La Tribu has been featured at Lincoln Center and El Museo del Barrio among many others. He is the recipient of a NYSCA Folk and Traditional Arts Apprenticeship Grant, City Parks Foundation grant, and NYFA City Artists Corps grant among others.Ghanaian-born artist Tijay Mohammed currently resides in Bronx, NY. As an artist he has a strong passion for exploring issues that affect community and humanity at large. His work explores the concept of 'excess' in the production and consumption of products, and offers a solution through the integration of materials reuse and up-cycling. Tijay has spearheaded workshops and community-oriented projects for esteemed organizations, including the Studio Museum Harlem, Brooklyn Museum, Sugar Hill Children’s Museum of Art & Storytelling, Children’s Museum of Manhattan, Wallach Art Gallery, Lehman College, University of Ghana, and Pinto Community Centre in Trinidad and Tobago.
events.venue: Enslaved Burial Ground (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.description: Inwood Canoe Club and Friends of Inwood Hill Park are recruiting volunteers to clean up our beloved Hudson River shoreline. We'll be collecting trash to keep our waterfront community clean. Trash bags, work gloves, latex gloves, and grabbers will be provided. Feel free to bring your own work gloves and water bottle.Be sure to complete your 2026 season waiver before you arrive at the boathouse. Inwood Canoe Club en asociación con Friends of Inwood Hill Park están reclutando voluntarios para limpiar nuestra querida orilla del río Hudson. Recogeremos basura para limpiar nuestra comunidad litoral. Proporcionaremos bolsas de basura, guantes de trabajo, junto con algunos guantes de látex y agarradores. Puedes traer tus propios guantes de trabajo y una botella de agua.No olvides completar tu formulario Smart Waiver antes de venir a Inwood Canoe Club.
events.venue: Inwood Canoe Club (in Inwood Hill Park),Inwood, west end of Dyckman Street, then south through the gate and past the sailing club. (in Inwood Hill Park)

events.title: Family Camping: Overnight at the Unisphere
events.description: The Urban Park Rangers celebrate the tradition of camping and we look forward to welcoming you. Join us for an unforgettable overnight camping adventure in Flushing Meadows Corona Park, home to the iconic Unisphere. Set up your tent, explore the park after dark, and enjoy an evening of campfire storytelling, s’mores, and more, all in the heart of Queens. No camping experience or equipment is required! Whether you’re a first-time camper or a seasoned outdoor explorer, join us for a rare chance to sleep under the stars in one of New York City’s most beloved parks. Each participant will take home a brand-new sleeping bag. Participants will be selected by lottery. Lottery registration period opens Thursday September 10 at 10:00 a.m. and closes Sunday September 13 at 11:00 p.m. Please Note:You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same Xplor Recreation account. Anyone who is not registered will not be permitted to attend.Selected participants will be notified via email on Monday September 14.

events.title: Ensemble in Process: The Medieval Chronicles
events.description: Part concert, part theatrical experience, Ensemble in Process presents The Medieval Chronicles which will take the audience through one's journey of ‘The Dark Night of The Soul’, weaving together a narrative of poetry, music and dance of the Medieval, Renaissance and Contemporary Eras. As we enter our own era unknown, join us for a celebration of some of the most beautiful and wise voices of the past and present as we seek to shine a little light in the dark.The Medieval Chronicles will feature music by Hildegard von Bingen, Thomas Tallis, William Purcell, Adam de la Halle, Derek David, Brian Mark, Missy Mazzoli, and Bjork, with texts integrated by poets William Blake, Maya Angelou, Rumi, Dylan Thomas, and Dante, among others. Performances by Brian Mark, Allyson Clare, Seth Gilman, Rose Hegele, Nick Pauly, Nathaniel Grohmann, and Andres Guerra. Narration: Seth Gilman. Dancers: Charlotte Aucella and Carol Chave. Please note, weather permitting, the beginning of the performance in Act I will commence on the outside stage, as the audience will accompany the narrator back inside the concert hall. At the end of Act III, the audience will follow the performers outside as the concert will therefore finish outdoors.

events.title: C-Words: Six New Short Plays Presented By Creative Women New York
events.description: Six plays, five writers, four directors, and an afternoon of theatre in the Field House! events.title: Tour the Historic Lawrence Cemetery
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society is conducting a free guided tour of the historic Lawrence Cemetery, the burial ground of one of Bayside's founding families. The cemetery's first burial occurred in 1832, with the most recent in 1939. Notable individuals who are interred here include Cornelius Van Wyck Lawrence, New York City's first popularly elected mayor, and Colonel Frederick Newbold Lawrence, former president of the New York Stock Exchange. In 1967, the NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Lawrence Cemetery as a landmark. History will come alive on our tour as we recount the stories of different members of the Lawrence family.Outside Meetup Location: This tour will take place at the Lawrence Cemetery in Bayside, which is located at the corner of 216th Street and 42nd Avenue. Please note:The site will require walking on uneven groundLong pants are recommended to protect your legsNo restrooms are available on siteParking by the Lawrence Cemetery is limitedThe cost is free. events.title: OHNY: Conference House Park Historic Houses
events.description: Staten Island, New York City, and the nation’s history and architecture are alive and present within the built environment of Conference House Park. On OHNY Weekend, in addition to the park’s namesake, the circa-1680 Conference House (Christopher Billop House), two other historic house interiors will be open to visitors. This includes the NYC landmark-designated Henry Hogg-Biddle House (circa 1840) with its front and rear two-story portico and the William H. Rutan House (aka The Rutan-Becket House) with its intact 1950s era kitchen, not usually open to the public. The maritime past of Staten Island’s south shore is highlighted by these wonderful historic buildings.Access to the historic house interiors require stairs. Trails, pathways, and sidewalks connect houses and may be uneven.Conference House Park may be reached by the S78 bus to the corner of Hylan Boulevard and Craig Avenue, or the Tottenville SIR station. A parking lot and nearby street parking are available.Open House New York Weekend is an annual festival that unlocks hundreds of destinations across the five boroughs for behind-the-scenes tours and special activities.

events.title: OHNY: Brougham Cottage Grounds at Blue Heron Park
events.description: Join the Open House New York 2026 Festival and explore the grounds of the Historic Brougham Cottage in Blue Heron Park!Located at 4746 Amboy Road, Staten Island, NY, and located within a wooded backdrop, the circa 1726 Brougham Cottage is a surviving Dutch H-frame home.Brougham Cottage survives as a rare example of the small vernacular farm houses that were once common in the 18th and early 19th century rural landscape and have all but disappeared. It is a significant example of Dutch-American design and a rare reminder of Staten Island’s rural history and its vernacular architectural traditions.

events.title: BHS Castle Tour
events.description: The Bayside Historical Society is excited to participate in this year's Open House New York Weekend, an event spanning all five boroughs that celebrates architecture and design.On Sunday, October 18th, from 12:00pm to 4:00pm, we will be participating with free guided tours of The Castle in Fort Totten Park, which has been the home of the Bayside Historical Society since 1984. Built in 1887, the building was originally used by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers as their Officers’ Mess Hall and Club. The Castle is one of the finest surviving examples in New York City of Gothic Revival castellated architecture, and is a NYC designated landmark that is also listed on the National Register of Historic Places.Our staff will be on hand to give tours and talk about our beautiful building and its history, along with the history of the land dating back to 1639. Guests can also explore the Bayside Historical Society's newest exhibition, "Home Front and Front Lines: 250 Years of American Service," which explores the stories of northeast Queens residents whose service, sacrifice, and civic engagement helped shape the American experience.Light refreshments will be provided. RSVP at www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/open-house-new-york-2026.

events.title: What do we need from our leaders?
events.description:
Once a month, we bring together a group for an accessible talk on philosophy and some well-structured conversation, with wine and bites in a cozy spot in Harlem.

Our goal is to recreate the best undergrad discussion course you ever attended and help you meet some people who want to have conversations about things that matter.

This October we're hosting Robert Gooding-Williams, the Brooks and Suzanne Ragen Professor of Philosophy at Yale and author of In the Shadow of Du Bois. We'll spend the evening discussing the questions: 

> what makes someone a progressive?
> do the most highly educated and well connected people have a duty to serve their communities?
> ultimately, what do we need for our leaders in order for our communities to prosper?

Here's how the night will go:

> [30 mins] Wine, apps, mingling
> [30 mins] talk from the professor
> [30 mins] breakout groups
> [30 mins] Q&A with the professor
> [as long as you want] continue your most interesting discussions

No pre-reading required, we’ll have a cheat sheet with the main ideas. Come alone or bring a friend, looking forward to seeing you there!

events.title: BRIC Jazzfest
events.description:
In alignment with BRIC’s year-long curatorial vision of bringing Radical Joy to life, BRIC JazzFest 2026 expands the circle of what we consider jazz and welcomes those who have yet to find their home within its tent. The lineup presents jazz as a collective experience, as regions to move through and music to dance to.

Across two nights, Arturo O’Farrill & the Afro-Latin Jazz Orchestra,Bilal, Mohini Dey, Braxton Cook, Sparklmami, Marcus Gilmore, Melvis Santa presents Gata Jazz, Takuya Kuroda, Salin, Tyreek McDole, and Laura Anglade move jazz into conversation with soul, R&B, funk, hip-hop, electronic music, rock, house, Afro-Caribbean traditions, Indian rhythms, Indigenous Thai instrumentation, and American standards. Together, they demonstrate that jazz remains most alive when it returns to its roots in freedom and improvisation while opening itself to new voices, new bodies, and new possibilities.

we'll be doing a light demo on some deeply basic embroidery techniques, and then you'll have two hours to bead and embellish your custom images or any fabric prints and scraps we provide.

events.title: October Bookclub “Monstrilio”
events.description:
What better way to celebrate Latine Heritage Month and spooky season than with a Latin American author's take on grief and monsters?

Join us this month as we discuss Gerardo Sámano Córdova's debut "Monstrilio," a dual-perspective literary/creature horror novel exploring grief, queerness, and acceptance.

A grieving mother tries to preserve a piece of her son by cutting up a little bit of his lung and storing it in a jar. Inspired by folklore and fueled by unimaginable sadness, she feeds and nurtures the lung until it becomes a living creature.

This book club is free and open to anyone wanting to discuss stories of those who have been historically underrepresented in literature. Can't wait to come together in community soon!

Also, we're using this month as a book swap opportunity since last month’s was rained out. Have any books you want to pass along? Bring em and maybe you'll find something new to come home with <3

events.title: Crimson & Gold: A Fall Walk in Central Park
events.description:
On October 24, we’re taking an autumn walk through Central Park, exploring some of the park’s most beautiful fall spots, iconic bridges, scenic paths, and colorful foliage. Join us for a relaxed afternoon stroll through the park, with plenty of opportunities to enjoy the scenery, take photos, and finish together at the Conservatory Garden.

📍 Meetup: Columbus Circle / 59th Street Entrance at 2:00 PM, by the M5 Bus Stop. We’ll spend 30 minutes mingling before beginning the walk at 2:30 PM.

Along the way, we’ll visit some of Central Park’s most scenic spots:

• The Pond & Gapstow Bridge - an iconic Central Park view surrounded by fall foliage, with beautiful reflections and photo opportunities.

• The Mall & Literary Walk - a scenic promenade lined with towering elm trees and a beautiful autumn canopy.

• Bethesda Terrace & Fountain + Bow Bridge - one of the park’s most iconic areas, with stunning architecture, views, and fall scenery. We’ll pause here for about 10 minutes.

• Cedar Hill - a peaceful hill surrounded by colorful trees and a quieter stretch of the park.

• Turtle Pond - a scenic spot with views of the surrounding foliage and reflections on the water. We’ll pause here for about 5 minutes.

• Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir - a scenic stretch with panoramic water views surrounded by autumn colors.

• North Meadow - an open area surrounded by trees, where we’ll stop for a group photo. We’ll pause here for about 5 minutes.

• Conservatory Garden - a beautiful six-acre formal garden in the northeast corner of the park and the final stop of our walk. Feel free to stay and enjoy the garden before heading home.

🚶 Walk: Approximately 2.5 miles at a relaxed pace (~2–2.5 hours)

🍂 Tips for Enjoying the Walk:
• Wear comfortable walking shoes
• Bring water

It’s free to join. Everyone 18+ is welcome 🎉

📸 Stay connected: Follow along on Instagram for future walks, food crawls, and event highlights:

https://www.instagram.com/nycfoodies.club

events.title: Fundraiser to Fight Deed Theft
events.description:
Input Output and  Cybersoul present Input x 

Cybersoul: Fundraiser to Fight Deed Theft, with help from our friends at Gays Get Political!

We’re throwing a party for the city we love, and raising money to help protect the people who make it home.

Deed theft is one of the quieter ways New Yorkers become targets for predatory real-estate practices. Through forged documents, deceptive contracts, or other forms of fraud, scammers can take control of someone’s home without their knowledge. For longtime homeowners, losing a deed can mean losing a home, a lifetime of equity, and generational wealth. And as neighborhoods change and property values rise, the stakes only get higher.

So we’re bringing together some of our favorite DJs and producers for a night of music and solidarity. 100% of profits will go to The Center for NYC Neighborhoods, supporting their work to protect homeowners and fight displacement across New York City.

Donations at the door and are suggested but not mandatory. Come dance and show some love for your neighbors

events.title: Llama & Alpaca-My-Appetite: Trail Side Taste Of Peru
events.description:
Trade city streets for open fields and fresh country air as we head out of town for a one-of-a-kind countryside escape. On this adventure, you won’t just be hiking! You’ll be trekking alongside llamas and alpacas, your new four-legged trail companions.

We’ll arrive at the farm, meet our fluffy hiking partners, and set off on a relaxed, scenic walk through rolling hills and peaceful landscapes. These gentle, curious animals make the experience equal parts calming and unforgettable (and yes: very Instagram-worthy).

After our trek, we’ll shift from trail time to taste time with a trail-side taste of Peru: a delicious nod to the animals’ South American roots. Expect a curated Peruvian-inspired food experience that brings bold flavors and countryside vibes together. Fresh air, good company, and incredible bites… this is the kind of pairing we like.

Whether you’re here for the animal energy, the cultural flavors, or just a wholesome day outside, this one hits on all levels. Fluffy hiking partners. Bold flavors. Countryside energy with a South American twist.

Event Details:
10:00 AM – Meet at The Standard Biergarten
10:30 AM – Depart NYC
12:00 PM – Arrive at Farm + Llama & Alpaca Trek
3:15 PM – Conclude Trek + Trail Side Taste of Peru
5:30 PM – Depart for NYC
7:00 PM – Arrive back in NYC
(All times are approximate and subject to traffic and group pace.)

What’s Included in Your Ticket:
Round-trip transportation
Guided farm hike
Llama & alpaca trekking experience
Beverages for the ride home
OUTSIDERS host on-site

What to Bring:
Proper hiking boots (required)
Plenty of water
Weather-appropriate layers
Big appetite
Card/cash for post-hike meal

Important Notes:
Proper hiking boots are required.
Our adventures are full-day experiences. We do not recommend scheduling other activities that day, as return times can vary.

Proper footwear is mandatory. Unsafe attire may result in denied participation for safety reasons.
If you are not dressed in weather-appropriate gear or your attire is deemed unsuitable for the activity, we have the right to turn you down for the safety of the group and yourself.

If you have any medical conditions or injuries that might prevent you from completing the trip, please consult your physician to confirm your ability to partake in the activities safely.
A signed waiver is required.

events.title: ‘Zero Sum’ - solo exhibition
events.description:
Pushup Gallery is pleased to announce “Zero Sum” a solo exhibition by Elizabeth Sundahl opening Saturday October 17th, 6-9 pm, 17-38 George Street Ridgewood NY.

Sundahl’s work recontextualizes familiar materials like paper mache, beeswax, colored pencil, and found objects into languishing, dream-like landscapes and interiors. Here, Sundahl examines the ways value is exchanged, consumed, obscured, and redistributed. This will be her first solo exhibition.
